description: Roll-up: N children billed under one parent budget must be summed against that budget for enforcement; a per-child check alone passes a set that is over budget in aggregate. Added 2026-10-26 after atharnouman's cross-walk found the gap (007b tests one child_spend).

vectors.name: Roll-up — N children against one parent budget
vectors.description: When N children bill under one parent budget, enforcement must sum every child's spend against the parent budget; per-child respect with aggregate overspend must FAIL.
vectors.principle: Per-child enforcement without an aggregate roll-up lets fan-out overspend a budget that every child individually respects.
source_evidence: a2aproject/A2A#2121 — budget propagation and roll-up across sibling delegations (cross-walk question 2)
steipete/CodexBar#3524 — fan-out inflation through inherited counters

vectors.description: Every child within its slice, the sum over the parent budget -> FAIL

expect.failure_reason: every child respects its slice; the sum of children exceeds the parent budget, which no per-child check sees. The allocation itself is over-subscribed (slices sum 1050 > 1000), so full slice use would always overspend — the roll-up catches the spend; the allocation gap mirrors LIP-3 section 6's issuer-side gap

vectors.description: Sum of children within the parent budget -> PASS

expect.note: PASS is a roll-up verdict only: it reads the cost reported up. Slice rules over the same allocation fail at issuance (350 x 3 = 1050 > 1000) — the over-subscription 008a shows late, 008b has not shown yet. Only the issuer closes the allocation gap (LIP-3 sec 6; atharnouman's split-verdict reading, 2026-10-26).
